questions.question: Dr. Chirif, a dentist practicing as a natural person, realizes a taxable profit of 250,000 DH. What would be the approximate tax advantage if he opted for an LLC subject to CIT?
options: A tax saving of about 10,000 to 15,000 DH
A tax saving of about 25,000 to 30,000 DH
A tax increase of about 5,000 DH
No significant difference between the two regimes
questions.explanation: From about 200,000 to 250,000 DH of profit, CIT (10% on the 0-300,000 DH bracket) becomes more advantageous than PIT (progressive scale up to 37%), generating a saving of about 25,000 to 30,000 DH.

questions.question: According to the 2026 Finance Law, what is the CIT rate applicable to companies whose net profit is less than 100 million DH?
questions.explanation: The 2026 Finance Law completes the unification of CIT rates with a single rate of 20% for companies whose net profit is less than 100 million DH.

questions.question: Dr. Falahi owns an LLC with a net profit of 250,000 DH. What will be the amount of CIT due according to the 2026 scale?
questions.explanation: For the 0 to 300,000 DH bracket, the CIT rate is 10%. The tax due is therefore 250,000 × 10% = 25,000 DH.

questions.question: According to the 2026 Finance Law, what is the withholding tax rate applicable to dividends distributed by an LLC in 2026?
questions.explanation: The 2026 Finance Law continues the programmed reduction of the withholding tax rate on dividends, set at 11.25% for 2026, with a target of 10% in 2027.

questions.question: Dr. Chirif owns an LLC with a net profit after tax of 300,000 DH, which he distributes as dividends. What will be the amount of withholding tax in 2026?
questions.explanation: The withholding tax on dividends in 2026 is 11.25%. The amount is therefore 300,000 × 11.25% = 33,750 DH.

questions.question: According to the 2026 Finance Law, what is the maximum marginal rate of PIT for a dentist practicing as a natural person?
questions.explanation: The 2026 Finance Law maintains the maximum marginal PIT rate at 37% for taxable net incomes exceeding 180,000 DH.

questions.question: According to the 2026 Finance Law, what is the PIT exemption threshold for a single dentist with no dependents?
questions.explanation: The 2026 Finance Law maintains the PIT exemption threshold at 40,000 DH of taxable net income, exempting salaries below 6,000 DH per month.

questions.question: According to the 2026 Finance Law, what is the annual tax reduction amount for family dependents per dependent?
questions.explanation: The 2026 Finance Law increased the annual reduction for family dependents from 500 to 600 DH per dependent, with a cap of 3,600 DH for 6 dependents.

questions.question: Dr. Falahi, a dentist practicing as a natural person, has 3 dependent children. What is the total amount of the tax reduction for family dependents he can deduct in 2026?
questions.explanation: The annual reduction is 600 DH per dependent × 3 children = 1,800 DH.

questions.question: According to the 2026 Finance Law, what is the normal rate of the Minimum Contribution for companies subject to CIT?
questions.explanation: Since the reform introduced by the 2023 Finance Law, the normal Minimum Contribution rate is 0.25% of turnover.

questions.question: Dr. Chirif owns an LLC with a turnover of 2,000,000 DH. What is the minimum amount of his Minimum Contribution?
questions.explanation: For companies subject to CIT, the Minimum Contribution cannot be less than 3,000 DH, even if 0.25% of turnover is below this amount.

questions.question: Dr. Falahi owns an LLC with a turnover of 1,000,000 DH. What is the amount of his Minimum Contribution at the normal rate?
questions.explanation: The normal rate is 0.25% of turnover, i.e. 2,500 DH. Since the minimum is 3,000 DH, this amount is due.

questions.question: Dr. Chirif created an LLC in January 2026. For how many months is it exempt from the Minimum Contribution?
questions.explanation: Newly created companies benefit from an exemption from the Minimum Contribution for their first 36 months of activity.

questions.question: According to the 2026 Finance Law, what is the reduced rate of the Minimum Contribution for certain essential products?
questions.explanation: A reduced rate of 0.15% applies to operations involving essential products (oil, gas, butter, oil, sugar, flour, water, electricity, medicines).

questions.question: Dr. Falahi, a natural person, has a turnover of 800,000 DH. What is the applicable Minimum Contribution rate?
questions.explanation: For natural persons subject to PIT, the Minimum Contribution rate is 6% of turnover.

questions.question: Dr. Chirif, a natural person, has a turnover of 800,000 DH and a taxable profit of 80,000 DH. Which tax will he pay if the Minimum Contribution exceeds the calculated PIT?
options: The higher amount between PIT and Minimum Contribution
No tax because the profit is low
questions.explanation: The taxpayer pays the higher amount between the calculated PIT and the Minimum Contribution. The Minimum Contribution for a natural person is 6% of turnover, i.e. 800,000 × 6% = 48,000 DH.

questions.question: According to the 2026 Finance Law, what is the CIT rate applicable to companies whose net profit exceeds 100 million DH?
questions.explanation: The 2026 Finance Law completes the unification of CIT rates with a rate of 35% for companies whose net profit is equal to or exceeds 100 million DH.

questions.question: Dr. Falahi owns an LLC with a net profit of 150,000 DH. What is the CIT rate applicable to this profit bracket?
questions.explanation: The CIT rate applicable to the taxable net profit bracket of 0 to 300,000 DH is 10%, regardless of the amount within this bracket.

questions.question: Dr. Chirif owns an LLC with a net profit of 2,000,000 DH. What is the amount of CIT due in 2026?
According to the 2026 Finance Law, what is the withholding tax rate on dividends in 2027 (target set by law)?
questions.explanation: The 2026 Finance Law continues the programmed reduction of the withholding tax rate on dividends to reach the target of 10% in 2027.

questions.question: Dr. Falahi sells his business in 2026 at the age of 67. According to the 2026 Finance Law, what reduction does he benefit from on the capital gain?
questions.explanation: Natural persons whose income is determined under the Single Professional Contribution regime benefit from a 50% reduction on the capital gain of intangible assets of the business, within the limit of 1,000,000 DH, provided they have reached at least 65 years of age.

questions.question: According to the 2026 Finance Law, are retirement pensions exempt from PIT starting in 2026?
options: Yes, total exemption from PIT for retirement pensions and free life annuities
Yes, but only for pensions below 10,000 DH
No, pensions remain subject to the progressive scale
questions.explanation: The 2026 Finance Law implements the total exemption from PIT for retirement pensions and free life annuities starting January 1, 2026.

questions.question: Dr. Chirif opts for the Single Professional Contribution. What is the applicable flat-rate tax rate?
questions.explanation: The Single Professional Contribution offers a flat-rate tax at 10% applied to a flat-rate profit determined on turnover, without deduction of actual expenses.

questions.question: According to the 2026 Finance Law, what is the net profit threshold from which companies are subject to the 35% CIT rate?
questions.explanation: The 2026 Finance Law completes the unification of CIT rates with a rate of 35% for companies whose net profit is equal to or exceeds 100 million DH. Below this threshold, the rate is 20%.

questions.question: Dr. Falahi creates an LLC in 2026. What is the main tax advantage of the LLC compared to practicing as a natural person for a profit of 200,000 DH?
options: No advantage, PIT is more favorable
A CIT rate of 10% on the first 300,000 DH bracket
A CIT rate of 20% on the entire profit
questions.explanation: For companies, CIT applies at 10% on the profit bracket of 0 to 300,000 DH, which is significantly more favorable than the progressive PIT scale which can reach 37% on the same income bracket.
